text:
megan: quick poll — how many of you have a decorative object (plant, gnome, lava lamp) that somehow turned into a wifi antagonist? sharing pic of my chaos: https://imgur.com/a/gh4t9 (gnome sitting on ethernet switch)
sam: lol that gnome looks like it’s plotting packet loss :rofl:
jordan: same. my ficus grew into the router antenna last month. signal dropped whenever it watered itself. :sweat_smile:
lee: in my case it was the monitor stand — magnetized cable clips + metal base = weird interference. moved the router 6 inches and it's night and day.
ravi: Pro tip: try 2.4GHz for devices with low range, 5GHz for laptop. Or just bribe the gnome with a tiny hat and move it 2ft.
olivia: vote: should we do a "show your WFH weird setup" thread tomorrow morning? :raised_hands:
megan: yes please. winners get virtual coffee & a sticker from ops. also curious — any quick fixes y'all swear by?
sam: Mesh nodes. Expensive but saved me.
jordan: doorstop under the router works for me (elevation = better line of sight).
lee: duct-tape triumph — cable tied up and router on top shelf. not pretty but stable. :grimacing:
ravi: if anyone wants I can run a quick speed test script and share results in the channel.
megan: that'd be awesome ravi, thanks. maybe include ping to our staging app too?
dev-bot: scheduled speed-check job queued by ravi at 2149997790 — results will post to #random when done.
olivia: obligatory gif: https://giphy.com/gifs/gnome-fail-3o6Zt8MgUuvSbkZYWc
megan: okay saving these tips — also attaching the photo since imgur is flaky: (image: gnome-on-switch.jpg)
sam: :thumbsup: (2)
jordan: can't wait for tomorrow's "weird setups" gallery. maybe we make it a biweekly thing?
lee: +1 for biweekly. could be good morale boost.
megan: agreed. closing poll: who will actually clean their desk before posting? :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye:
participants poll replies: megan: maybe, sam: nope, jordan: probably not, lee: maybe, ravi: yes, olivia: maybe
